note: The 160 unvoiced lines of the 7 October 2026 audit (every spoken line the games were reading with browser text-to-speech). One take per line, generated in ElevenLabs flow kvzIYLAVhQxuu2koUOll; takes were saved as <key>.mp3 and ingested with scripts/neonoire/voice-batch.mjs. gap = seconds of silence after the previous line (first line of a frame: absolute offset). replace = an older take of the same moment re-recorded under its old id (the old take stays in the line's history); retire = an older take archived (docs/neonoire/voice/archive/*-cut-*.mp3) and dropped from the manifest. voice = the ElevenLabs voice the take was made with. frameOrder = the playing order of the frames that mix new takes with existing ones. Never use [quietly], [softly] or [whispers] tags with Jack and Vera: they read as whispers (about 10 dB under their speaking level).

lines.prompt: [steadily] After twenty years.
[dryly] Who calls me that?
[gently] Go to sleep, Jack. You found enough twenty years ago. You're too old to be haunted.
[cheerfully] Thank you very much.
[thoughtfully] She wasn't planning to disappear.
[wryly] Take this too. It's mine. She stole it.

[urgently] They have my purse. My passport. They know my name. They know where I live, where she lives, all of it. If she knows where I am, she'll come here. She won't be able to help it. And they'll follow her. [pause] They'll use her to get to me. And then they'll kill her too.
[quietly] I believe he was sad. I don't know if I believe the rest. [pause] A man wrote to me last week. He said Dad didn't do it. He said the police knew.
[tearfully] He knew me. He saw me in the doorway and stopped. And at the end he pressed the key into my hand. "Don't let them have it."
[evenly] Show me where.
[quietly] Every January. Cash, in an envelope. Twenty years. Even after he left, the receipts kept coming here.
[evenly] The coast. An inn off the highway. The phone is pink.
[curious] The girl?
[evenly] Safe. Tomorrow it'll be over.
[bitterly] You said that about my daughter.
[politely] Shitsurei shimasu.
[warmly] Vera? Honey?
[calling out] Vera?
[drowsily] You're the first person I've trusted since she disappeared.
[evenly] Shiohama. Third visit. The residents say men came in the spring with flowers, and then in the summer with iron bars. The fire began in two places at once. Fires don't do that.
[evenly] The claim will be paid. Everyone wants it paid. The company, the police, the man who owns the land now. Kurose. Always Kurose.

[quietly] The police have given me a young detective who speaks English. They call him Jack. He's bright. He believes me. We ate noodles at Kaneko's and I told him everything and he wrote it all down.
[quietly] Today Jack signed the report. Accidental fire. I don't blame him. He is twenty-eight years old and they own his whole life. But I thought, of all of them, he would stand with me.
[tired] I'll go on alone. I've done it before.

[quietly] They followed me home again tonight. The girls were asleep. I stood at the door a long time. [pause] If something happens to me, it will not be what they say. Tell Vera. When she is old enough. Tell her it will not be what they say.
[evenly] Nine o'clock. A grey car. Your driver.
[flatly] Only you knew.
[gently] You told me yourself, Jack. [pause] You always tell the wrong person.
[evenly] Twenty years ago. Daniel. Was that you?
[gently] I have never killed anyone in my life. [pause] I only ever told people where to find them.
[calmly] Where is it? Sakai's thing.
[puzzled] The girl?
[gruffly] There are still people in the building. Old people. They won't sign.
[calmly] The building must be empty by the end of the month.
[gruffly] And if it isn't?
[calmly] Then it will be empty in a different way. [pause] Don't make me say it more clearly, Sakai. I don't like to repeat myself.
[gravely] That's Kurose.
[flatly] That's Kurose.
[dryly] A voice on a twenty-year-old tape. His lawyers will say it's a fake. They'll say Sakai was a gangster with a grudge.
[evenly] Then you'll need a witness.

[quietly] Twenty years ago I was a police detective. An American insurance investigator named Daniel Voss proved the Shiohama fire was arson. I believed him. I was ordered to close the case, and I signed a report saying the fire was an accident. [pause] Weeks later he was found dead. I didn't ask any questions.
[evenly] You understand what you're saying. You'll be named. Your part too.
[firmly] Start with my part.
[gently] From the beginning.
[evenly] Two hours. He hasn't stopped.
[gently] I know. I can see.
[evenly] Every page. Then the original goes in the safe downstairs, and nobody touches it. Including you.
[sadly] It's all I have of him.

[evenly] Then I will take care of it. [pause] Kondo's files were in his desk. Six months of redevelopment money, and Kurose's name in most of it. And the grey car that left the Hive last night was found burnt out in Adachi at dawn. Registered to a security company. The company belongs to Kurose Development. [pause] Tomorrow we put it to them for comment. They will refuse to see a reporter.
[evenly] I'll go.
[firmly] That is not your job.
[evenly] It isn't yours either. He'll see me. [pause] He'll want to look at me.
[evenly] The copies. Not the original.
[gently] When my secretary said the daughter of Daniel Voss wanted to see me, I didn't believe her.
[evenly] He sat where you're sitting. He looked at me the way you are. As if I'd done something.
[evenly] Did you?
[calmly] To him? I don't remember. [pause] Your father was a good man, Miss Voss. I mean that sincerely. There are not many. [pause] Good men are very expensive.
[calmly] What is it you want?
[evenly] The Toto Shimbun will print tomorrow. They asked me to bring you the chance to reply.
[evenly] I said I'd come.
[curious] Why?
[evenly] I wanted to see your face.
[firmly] It's just a face.
[evenly] My father kept notes. He wrote your name on every page. [pause] And now I know.
[dryly] It's very clean.
[calmly] Follow her.
[gruffly] Someone for you.
[evenly] She asked me to come. Kaneko. She said I should see where Mara was.
[gently] That's me.
[tenderly] She drew it after you left.
[sadly] She was here. The day I came.
[flatly] Three feet away.
[bitterly] And you told her not to come out.
[sadly] She told herself. [pause] She was protecting you. So was I.
[evenly] Ishida called me before it was on any news. He knew exactly where she was.
[quietly] I told him. [pause] Where she'd be, and when. He arranged the car. It was his driver. That's mine.
[evenly] I told you about the detective. The one who promised a car. You never asked who.
[flatly] No.
[firmly] I'm not going to tell you it wasn't yours.
[pleading] Don't.
[tenderly] She drew what she saw. All of it.
[sadly] She never told me she'd kept them.
[evenly] I'm taking these to Harada. Somebody has to look at them. [pause] I read his notebook.
[evenly] I know.
[gently] He didn't blame you.
[heavily] I know.
[hesitantly] I don't know if I'm as good as he was.
[gently] I'm not asking you to be.
[curtly] Position.
[urgently] Up. Through the back. The stairs by the dentist. Then go through the neighbours. Everyone will open a door.
[evenly] I know them.
[urgently] Come with us.
[dryly] I have lived here fifty years. They can come and find me.
[urgently] Go now. They will help you.
[urgently] Is Kaneko —
[evenly] The Hive looks after its own.
[sadly] Mara was safe here. Until us.
[gently] It's only tea.
[evenly] Yes. [pause] Where? [pause] In his own car. Under the expressway. Sitting up, engine off. No marks. [pause] He left a statement.
[evenly] Harada says the prosecutors want you to testify.
[evenly] Yes.
[evenly] And your licence?
[dryly] Gone. [pause] It should have gone twenty years ago.
[evenly] Ishida left a statement. He acted alone.
[dryly] Is that what it says?
[dryly] That's what the police say it says.
[evenly] Harada has Mara's drawings. The pages from the floor of the bar. She says they're the only eyewitness there is.
[tenderly] She'd have liked that. Being asked.
[firmly] Nobody asked her. She drew it anyway.
[gently] This is yours.
[gently] She said your father gave it to her. She said you only claim it was yours.
[voice breaking] Liar. It was mine.
[heavily] At the end, she asked me to tell you something.
[tenderly] She said to tell you she was sorry.
[sadly] I couldn't say anything in the rain.
[gently] No. [pause] Neither could I.
[wistfully] I don't know what we are.
[earnestly] Neither do I.
[dryly] I still have your lighter.
[gently] I know.
[warmly] Kaneko's opening a new place. Near the station, under the arches. She's taking the sign.
[warmly] She says she opens at six.
[desperately] Is she okay? Is she — does she know you're —
[dryly] And they sent you.
[dryly] Is that what you were holding?
[dryly] It's what I had.
[evenly] Forty metres. [short pause] Twenty minutes. You never once lost me.
[curious] Is that bad?
[dryly] It's what a professional does.
[curious] Who did you think I was?
[dryly] Somebody who'd be worse company.
[evenly] You said you'd look. You didn't say where. I waited outside your office.
[evenly] If you can follow me, so can they.
[gently] I brought food.
[tired] Park round the corner, then get in mine. [short pause] One car is a man waiting. Two is somebody watching.
[dryly] You were eating one when I came in. I assumed it was a lifestyle.
[dryly] This is a stakeout. Nothing happens.
[gently] Then I won't miss anything.
[curious] What are we waiting for?
[evenly] Whoever comes back.
[evenly] Back?
[evenly] Someone came back to this street that night. [short pause] Nobody comes back for what they already have.
[curious] What didn't they have?
[evenly] I don't know yet.
[gently] Is that for luck?
[dryly] It's so I don't lose it.
[weakly] I told her she always runs.
[evenly] You said.
[voice breaking] It's the last thing I —

[evenly] Runners don't pack. They leave with what they're wearing. Your sister had a suitcase zipped under the bed and a flight booked home. [pause] [gently] Whatever happened to her, she wasn't running from you.
[pleading] You don't know that.
[evenly] No. [pause] But I'd bet on it.
[curious] Is that routine? Watching a bar after a shooting?
[evenly] Probably.
[evenly] You don't think so.
[dryly] I think it's a plate number.
[evenly] Call me when you go somewhere.
[evenly] I will.
[dryly] That's a lie.
[flatly] Yes.
